headline: Two affordable housing proposals on former TPS school sites head to Toledo Plan Commission Nov. 5 — $20M+ AOA senior apartments and nine Habitat homes
paragraphs: Two affordable housing proposals using former Toledo Public Schools properties are scheduled to go before the Toledo City Plan Commission on November 5, 2026 — part of the broader effort to repurpose TPS buildings that became available through the district's Transformation Plan 2.0 restructuring, which closed several schools to address a $68 million deficit. The Blade reported both proposals on October 27, 2026.

The larger project involves the Area Office on Aging of Northwestern Ohio (AOA), in partnership with Lucas Metropolitan Housing Authority, NeighborWorks Toledo Region, and Community Building Partners. AOA has a deal to acquire the former TPS administration building — described as the Thurgood Marshall building — for $1, and proposes converting it into 86 units of affordable senior apartments combining the renovated historic structure with a new annex on former playfields and parking lots. All units would be available to seniors earning no more than 60% of area median income. The estimated investment is more than $20 million; the project has been supported by pre-development financing from LISC Toledo. After Plan Commission review, the proposal would advance to Toledo City Council.

The second proposal involves Habitat for Humanity and the former Beverly Elementary School site at Rugby Drive and Copland Boulevard. The Toledo Public Schools district has a tentative purchase agreement with Habitat for a nine-home, owner-occupied single-family development on the site. Two homes would be sold on the open market; the remaining homes would be offered through an affordable-purchase program. Both proposals face Plan Commission review on November 5 before advancing to council.
why_it_matters: Both projects represent the adaptive-reuse track for TPS surplus properties — the path that stabilizes neighborhood fabric by converting closed school buildings and sites into community assets rather than leaving them vacant or demolishing them. The AOA project's $20M+ scale makes it a significant affordable senior housing investment at a moment when Toledo's housing development pipeline is dominated by market-rate and ownership products. The Habitat project at Beverly Elementary extends the district's asset-to-homes conversion model beyond the Harvard Elementary effort underway in south Toledo. Plan Commission approval on November 5 would be the next milestone for both.
